title: Towaoc Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Towaoc wells have a median depth of 85 feet, but costs and yields vary by ground conditions and location.
h1: Towaoc, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost Guide
intro_html:
Buying land or a home near Towaoc means looking past the presence of a well. The useful questions are how deep nearby wells go, how much water they produce, and what a new well may cost on the specific parcel.

This page summarizes Colorado Division of Water Resources permit records for wells within 12 miles of Towaoc in Montezuma County. The records include 402 wells, but reporting is incomplete: 205 are recorded as constructed, 238 report total depth, 32 report pump yield, and only 5 report static water level.

sections.heading: Towaoc well depths reflect shallow local records, with exceptions
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Towaoc is 85 feet. The middle half runs from 30 to 160 feet, so many wells are relatively shallow, but the spread matters when pricing a new hole. A driller should not bid every parcel from the median alone.

Depth records show 53% of wells under 100 feet, 37% from 100 to 300 feet, 9% from 300 to 600 feet, and 2% at 600 feet or more. The deepest recorded well is 1,108 feet. Most permits identify an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer, with smaller numbers in the Mancos and Alluvial aquifers. Mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground can change quickly across a short distance.

sections.heading: Expected well yield around Towaoc
sections.html:
Reported yields are generally useful, but the sample is limited to 32 wells. The median pump yield is 10.9 gallons per minute, and the middle half is 4.9 to 15.0 gallons per minute.

The records show 3% of wells under 1 gallon per minute, 22% from 1 to 5, 38% from 5 to 15, and 38% above 15 gallons per minute. That distribution gives a buyer a reasonable local range, not a guarantee for a particular lot. A low-yield well may still serve a household with storage, while a higher-yield result provides more operating margin. Confirm the permitted use and test the well before relying on it for a home, livestock, or other demands.

sections.heading: Water levels near Towaoc look shallow, but the trend is limited
sections.html:
Only 5 wells in the records report a static water level, so this is the weakest part of the local dataset. Among those reports, the median depth to water is 12 feet, with the middle half from 6 to 25 feet.

That small sample does not establish a reliable water-table trend. The permit history spans the 1960s through the 2020s, with the newest permit issued in 2025, but permit age is not the same as a measured water-level series. Do not assume the water table is stable or declining based on these records alone. Ask for the well construction report, static level measurement, pumping test, and any current service information for the property under contract.

sections.heading: Who has drilled near Towaoc, and when
sections.html:
Permit activity near Towaoc is spread across several decades. The records show 1 permit in the 1960s, 18 in the 1970s, 57 in the 1980s, 54 in the 1990s, 41 in the 2000s, 96 in the 2010s, and 40 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025.

The most active names in these records are Authorized (Pe, Pg), with 62 wells; Kilby'S Water Well Service (Kilby, Edward E), with 49; and Mcpherson Drilling Co. (Mcpherson, Billy G.), with 24. These counts describe permit records, not endorsements or current availability. Before hiring, verify licensing, insurance, references, and whether the driller has recent experience with the ground and access conditions on your parcel.

sections.heading: What a new Towaoc well may cost
sections.html:
For the mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground described in the cost model, the typical drilling rate is $50 to $75 per foot. At the local median depth of 85 feet, the drilled hole works out to about $4,200 to $6,400.

A finished system is more than the hole. Including the pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical work, the modeled total is about $10,200 to $18,400 at that median depth. A deeper-than-expected hole, difficult access, casing or grout requirements, water treatment, or extra trenching can move the price outside that range. Get a written bid that separates drilling, casing, grouting, development, pump equipment, electrical work, and testing.

sections.heading: Risks to check before building near Towaoc
sections.html:
Yield and contamination deserve separate review. Within about 10 miles, the mapped inventory includes 12 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 5 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Those mapped locations do not prove that a parcel's well is affected, but they are reasons to check the well history and obtain laboratory testing before closing.

Low-yield wells and dry holes remain possible, especially because most permits identify fractured-bedrock conditions and the records do not report results for every well. Confirm casing, grout, pump capacity, and water-quality testing. Locate the septic system and replacement area before finalizing a building site. Colorado well permits control allowed use; an exempt household-use well is subject to its permit terms and the 35-gpm exempt-well pumping limit. In an over-appropriated basin, an augmentation plan may be needed.

sections.heading: A practical plan for a Towaoc lot
sections.html:
Start with the neighboring wells closest to the parcel, giving priority to construction reports rather than map symbols alone. Compare their depths, yields, aquifer descriptions, static levels, and completion dates. The nearby communities of Cortez, Lewis, Dolores, Mancos, Marvel, and Hesperus can provide broader context, but conditions at the lot should control the decision.

For an existing home, inspect the pump, pressure tank, electrical components, storage, and treatment equipment, then collect a current water sample. For vacant land, confirm the water-rights path and permit before spending on excavation or house plans. Have a driller review access and a septic professional review soils and layout together. Keep a contingency for a deeper hole or lower yield instead of budgeting only from the 85-foot median.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Towaoc, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported depth near Towaoc is 85 feet, and the middle half runs from 30 to 160 feet. About 53% are under 100 feet, while 2% are 600 feet or deeper. The deepest recorded well is 1,108 feet, so nearby records should guide a parcel-specific bid rather than treating 85 feet as a guarantee.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Towaoc?
faq.a: The local cost model uses $50 to $75 per foot. At the 85-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $4,200 to $6,400. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $10,200 to $18,400. Actual cost can change with depth, access, casing, grout, and site layout.

faq.q: How much water do Towaoc wells produce?
faq.a: Among the 32 wells reporting pump yield, the median is 10.9 gallons per minute and the middle half is 4.9 to 15.0 gallons per minute. The records show 3% under 1 gallon per minute and 38% above 15. These figures describe reported wells, not a guarantee for a new well or an existing pump system.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Towaoc?
faq.a: The records alone cannot establish that a specific Towaoc well is safe to drink. Within about 10 miles are 12 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 5 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Have the well tested through a qualified laboratory, review nearby environmental information, and test again after changes to the well or property.

faq.q: Can I build a home on a well near Towaoc?
faq.a: A home may be possible, but confirm the Colorado Division of Water Resources permit and allowed use before buying or designing. Check well yield, septic separation and replacement areas, access, electrical needs, and water quality. An exempt household-use well is subject to its permit terms and the 35-gpm pumping limit; an augmentation plan may apply in an over-appropriated basin.
